notes:
History-video workflow: Create an introduction and subtitled original from historic speeches, interviews, broadcasts and archive footage. Plan the brief, track sources and licences, refresh end-card credits and remove replaced bakes. Review remains required before baking and export unless the user explicitly requests self-check and export. Deliveries can include a proofread transcript and an uncertainty table.
Old recordings: Measure loudness and processing delay, level recordings and quote clips, check trims against chapter positions, waveform offsets and printed durations, and preserve non-speech lead-ins unless cutting was approved. Lossy web recordings use a light restoration pass by default; stronger denoising requires a listening comparison and user choice.
Production scripts: Prepend introductions while shifting clips and chapters, merge timeline caption documents into language-specific SRT files, subset fonts, time original quotes and collect source credits. Add deliberate @beat pauses, continuous ambient motion across scene bundles, eased camera and spring helpers, audio envelopes, watermarks and music endings aligned to the final title card.
Caption controls: Agents can select no current-word effect, a color highlight or a palette-colored KTV sweep through captions_create style and setCaptionStyle. Sweep settings preserve other text motion and remain mutually exclusive with the current-word highlight.
LAN model API: Opt in to IPv4 LAN access for the OpenAI-compatible model API in Services or with services configure model-api --lan on. Bearer authentication remains required; public sources, browser Origins and DNS Host names are refused. LAN addresses appear in status and the interface; the Web page and MCP keep their existing access scope.
Project management: Remove a project registration and its sessions from BaoCut while keeping its folder and media on disk. Running turns stop first; removal is refused while a project video is open elsewhere. Missing folders are flagged, blocked from new work and skipped by default project selection instead of being silently recreated. Reopening a removed folder restores its project identity, but not removed sessions.
Caption templates: Adjust colors, fonts, font scale and supported constant positions, restore the original template, tag keywords and generate a new variant in the inspector. Scene summaries expose layers, timing and adjustable properties. Capability-gated scenes gain dynamic paint colors and blur, word-to-display-text projection, reference geometry, local layer captures and expression preconditions. Leading whitespace in transcribed words no longer breaks cue matching. The broader style library, style packs and layered look editor remain prototype-only.
Session files: Project-less sessions now use the system Videos or Movies folder under BaoCut, with migration from the old application-data Sessions directory. Desktop exports default to the configured save location or Downloads. Startup cleanup preserves unrelated user files.
Transparent media: Alpha composition bakes use lossless PNG in MOV, falling back to ProRes 4444 only when the PNG encoder is unavailable; opaque bakes retain ProRes 422 HQ. Transparent video and image overlays no longer add a black background plate over lower tracks.
Browser fonts and image providers: Web editor and review sessions can resolve installed local fonts for preview. Compatible image endpoints can return data URLs or HTTP(S) image URLs when base64 data is absent; API credentials are sent only to the configured endpoint origin, and non-image responses are rejected.
Requirements and verification limits: macOS packages require Apple Silicon and macOS 14+ and are signed and notarized. Windows CPU, CUDA and Vulkan packages are unsigned and require AVX2 and the Microsoft Visual C++ v14 x64 Redistributable; GPU variants require compatible drivers. ffmpeg/ffprobe and an agent engine remain external dependencies. Electron 44.9.3 embeds Node 24.22.0 and does not include the October Node security fixes. Automated checks do not cover full UI/export workflows, live model or GPU inference, physical IME candidate windows or paid agent calls.
